Review date: 2026-10-24

Evidence and reproducibility

All three originals were scanned with atomscan --no-update --analyze local
--mode slow -f json and cleave facts. No specimen was executed. The evidence
root is /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-28a4cdc2/scratch/analysis.
It contains before/after JSON, complete facts, token-resolved IL for all 301
managed methods, call/string listings, the 12 extracted resources, original
publisher downloads with their .forage.json provenance, and regression reports.
The independently recovered IL was also compared with the existing full ILSpy
output in the named scratch/triage/launcher.cs. Existing recovered game sidecars
were checked against the newly retrieved manifest before using their analysis.

96082e1bb5350495ce83fe6ad1c26cfde4c31171c0f200bc68585d2d08f3d9ef
Identity: Ultimate Metin2 / Ultimate Gems Cloud WinForms game launcher.
Verdict: BENIGN; assessment of this artifact, routed to sighted quarantine.

Main opens the visible launcher by default. Other branches require explicit
self-test, preview, update-apply, or recovery arguments. PlayGame starts the
local executor.exe. CheckUpdate calls Prepare, copies the current launcher to
an update helper, and launches it with --apply, a plan path, and the parent PID.
The helper waits for the old process, acquires an update lock, validates paths,
backs up/replaces allowed game files, and supports rollback/recovery. Hidden
windows belong to these helper launches, not an unseen shell or injected code.

Prepare reads the external gems_update.json. It requires an enabled HTTPS
channel, downloads Builds/latest-v2.json and the indicated manifest, and checks
SHA-256, sizes, schema, product, runtime-file allowlists, free space and whether
the game is closed. Local rejects traversal, reserved DOS names and reparse
points. RuntimePath rejects account/password/credential paths; these strings
are safeguards, not harvesting. COM1..COM9 occur in the reserved-name rejection.
Download disables automatic redirects and enforces response-length limits.
ServicePointManager selects TLS 1.2. Browser links are HTTPS and allowlisted.
Registry access stores Language and Motion under HKCU Software/UltimateMetin2/
GemsLauncher. It does not register login persistence. AppDomain.CurrentDomain
supplies BaseDirectory, not reflective invocation or an assembly payload.

All 12 managed resources are artwork or JSON catalogs. Nine PNGs have valid
chunk CRCs, end at IEND, and contain zero trailing bytes. Compressed image data
accounts for the large high-entropy code/resource measurements. C2PA metadata
inside some images is not an executed stage. No encoded executable, Assembly.Load
activation, remote command dispatch, credential theft or persistence was found.

Fresh retrieval of the update index and manifest from patch.ultimatemt2.com
succeeded. The index SHA-256 validates the manifest. Its GemsCloudLauncher.exe
entry names exactly the submitted hash, and a fresh download independently
reproduced all original bytes. The game website identifies itself as Metin2
Ultimate. The live content catalog is ordinary quests/events data; the weekly
calendar endpoint currently returns 404. Retrieved sidecars executor.exe,
UltimateGeoAudio.exe, endpoint INI and gems_update.json also match this manifest.
The native executor's game-client and anti-cheat capabilities are not attributed
to the launcher. The previously decompiled GeoAudio helper sends version, an
ephemeral session ID and client label to a pinned HTTPS endpoint, validates a
bounded country/language/IP JSON response, and caches localization data. Its
response handling does not evaluate remote code or record audio.

Verified publisher-hosted bytes, coherent game/update UI and restrictive update
handling tip the balance toward benign. The unsigned 0.0.0.0 build, blank metadata,
huge compressed resources and self-copy/helper execution plausibly explain generic
ML detections and collection. The exact historical deployment, sidecar settings,
user authorization and the source's reason for collecting it remain unknown.
Publisher-byte agreement alone is not a blanket endorsement of the game package.

4371bf1da65ce9540854824747acf4fe14e911982ecd8bf4c7decb43729a09d9
Identity: 189-byte firewall-style same-origin HTML redirect.
Verdict: BENIGN; assessment of the recovered response, not its unknown target.

The complete GBK-decoded document assigns window.location to
/haha.js?jdfwkey=1531 and offers the identical link with Chinese text meaning
that the user should click if automatic redirection does not occur. It contains
no obfuscation, decoder, script import, ActiveX, local execution or payload bytes.
Navigating to a .js pathname is not itself executing its response as a script.
The source filename is a collector label, not evidence of a Trojan capability.

The jdfwkey navigation scheme is consistent with Jindun anti-CC challenges.
A hosting provider describes generating JavaScript redirects with that parameter:
https://www.kkidc.com/helpcenter/detail/hcid/174/id/332.html
This is corroboration of a common mechanism, not proof of the exact provider.
Forager identified a historical Triage record, but additional metadata retrieval
returned HTTP 401. Neither the bytes nor recovered metadata supplies an origin
host, so the relative target cannot truthfully be fetched or assigned a domain.
A firewall response collected while fetching an allegedly malicious JS resource
is a plausible mislabel explanation. The original requested resource could
still have been hostile; its behavior is outside this recovered artifact.
Both accurate existing navigation/markup findings remain unchanged.

35b30c2713cc1aef3c5295bd1ee101132a65bb1a84cd3aa1665b3d2d2895146c
Identity: 88-byte HTML disk-image delivery redirector (#A002.html in feed data).
Verdict: MALICIOUS, from the balance of behavior and malware-corpus provenance.

The entire document is a zero-second meta refresh to an absolute HTTPS URL:
energom3d.hu/wp-admin/YU/A002.iso. Opening it requests the remote disk image
without a click or explanatory UI. An executable container served beneath a
WordPress administration path, immediate unattended navigation and the supplied
hostile provenance together tip the judgment toward malicious delivery. This
is an inference; the path does not itself prove a compromised WordPress site.

Forager attempted the exact ISO URL with retries; DNS resolution fails. Further
Triage metadata retrieval returned HTTP 401. No ISO contents, archive members,
mounting, process execution, persistence, exfiltration or family identity are
claimed. The wrapper contains no script, hidden encoding or further local stage.

Coverage goal: 0 hostile / 0 suspicious becomes 0 hostile / 1 suspicious. The
new detector binds the zero-delay refresh directive to an ISO target under the
CMS admin path. It is suspicious because this delivery shape is unusual but
could be legitimate in isolation. No evidence supports three independent hostile
behaviors or an activation chain. The unavailable image prevents analysis of its
possible execution, staging after download, persistence or theft. Existing archive-
URL, automatic download and navigation findings already cover the file's other
observable actions. No duplicate objectives or artificial hostile upgrades were
added to meet a count. The remaining limitation is unavailable downstream bytes
and insufficient static evidence for an intent-specific hostile rule, not a
reason to call ordinary redirect primitives hostile.

Rule changes and placement audit

Four notable reference observations were added: OpenSubKey in registry access,
FileStream in file opening, set_SecurityProtocol in TLS initialization, and
get_BaseDirectory in process self-path information. Each matches an exact name
in the PE code section and describes a reference, not proven runtime success,
selected protocol version, read/write access mode or bound data flow.

The unsigned filename-mismatched AppDomain composite moved from metaprogramming/
reflection to process/interpreter/runtime/clr. Its full matcher, exclusions,
criticality, confidence and type/platform scope are unchanged. Both exact
consumers (zero-width single-file carrier and zero-width MSIL exfil stub) now
reference the new ID. A structural comparison verifies that these are their
only changes. No source ancestor selectors consume this rule. The destination's
broad interpreter consumer is Python-only Empire generator logic; it cannot
consume this PE/DLL-only observation. The shortened description retains the
same claim. No rule was weakened, suppressed or reduced in severity.

The new suspicious HTML rule requires the ISO target within the zero-delay
refresh content itself and excludes HTML comments. It uses neither the specimen
hash, collected filename, hostname, arbitrary directory token nor image basename.
A delayed redirect, ordinary download path, unrelated nearby link, commented tag
and .iso.html extension are negative controls. The current bounded matcher covers
the conventional double-quoted attribute order present in this artifact; other
quote/order/query variants are not claimed as covered.

Comparison and retained coverage

Sample          Hostile       Suspicious    Calibrated ML      ML probability
96082e1bb535    0 -> 0        0 -> 0        BENIGN -> BENIGN   .740213 -> .730864
4371bf1da65c    0 -> 0        0 -> 0        BENIGN -> BENIGN   .0000409 unchanged
35b30c2713cc    0 -> 0        0 -> 1        BENIGN -> BENIGN   .0000650 -> .902965

The ISO remains a calibrated ML miss despite its now-visible suspicious finding.
The benign assessments agree with ML. Model v18 warns that its feature schema
is older than the engine's expected v21; no rule was inflated to alter a score.
Only the old AppDomain ID disappears from the launcher; the identical finding
remains under its correct runtime ID. All other findings and severities are
retained, with the four new notable references. There are no material detection
losses. All 12 manually extracted resources have identical before/after finding
sets and zero hostile/suspicious findings. Originals expose no archive-member
analysis tree; extracted resources are reported separately, not as a fetched ISO.

Fifteen production-path regression controls passed. The outside-batch real Salat
specimen (605aae2d9f1e499f2183b2412baf7748a3c69d5659740bc34914af02b6ae26af)
retains every original finding, including 9 hostile and 2 suspicious. Both the
resource and Salat comparisons use the unchanged HEAD rule snapshot as baseline.

scan-comparison.json records the original-file changes. check.py reproduces the
focused controls using a scratch directory and optional original launcher path.
The final repository gate is make validate, run after writing judgment markers.
